correctness.rationale: The proof is sound. Arc excess two forces either one outdegree-3 branch vertex or two outdegree-2 branch vertices. Eliminating deterministic chains gives exact first-return Perron equations. In the one-branch case, exponent transfer maximizes the return sum at \(1,2,m-1\) with loops and \(2,2,m-2\) without loops, with equality forcing internally disjoint covering excursions. The three irreducible endpoint patterns for two branch vertices yield strict inequalities at the candidate roots, so no two-branch graph attains the bound.
